entities.name: Talaromycosis
entities.description: A life-threatening systemic opportunistic fungal infection caused by the thermally dimorphic fungus Talaromyces marneffei, predominantly affecting severely immunocompromised individuals (notably advanced HIV with CD4 < 100 cells/uL and patients with anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies) in endemic Southeast Asia and southern China, characterized by reticuloendothelial dissemination and umbilicated necrotic papules.

entities.name: Endemic Residence or Travel in Southeast Asia and Southern China
entities.description: Strict geographic restriction to tropical and subtropical Southeast Asia and southern China, including northern and central Thailand, northern Vietnam, southern China (Guangxi, Guangdong, Yunnan), Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Taiwan, and northeastern India (Manipur).

entities.name: Agricultural Soil and Bamboo Rat Habitat Exposure During Rainy Season
entities.description: Environmental exposure to agricultural soil and burrows of endemic bamboo rats (Rhizomys pruinosus, Cannomys badius), with marked transmission peaks during the monsoon/rainy season.

entities.name: Aerosol Inhalation of Environmental Conidia
entities.description: Primary route of transmission involving inhalation of aerosolized environmental infectious conidia from disturbed soil into the pulmonary alveoli.

entities.name: Advanced HIV Infection with CD4 Count Below 100 cells/uL
entities.description: Severe cell-mediated immunosuppression from advanced HIV infection, representing 80-90% of clinical cases, typically presenting with CD4 T-lymphocyte counts below 50-100 cells/uL.

entities.name: High-Titer Neutralizing Anti-Interferon-Gamma Autoantibodies
entities.description: Acquired adult-onset immunodeficiency syndrome in non-HIV Asian adults caused by high-titer neutralizing autoantibodies against interferon-gamma, predisposing to severe, refractory disseminated talaromycosis with frequent osteoarticular and intestinal involvement.

entities.name: Secondary Immunosuppression from Hematological Malignancies and Targeted Immunosuppressants
entities.description: Non-HIV immunocompromised states including hematological malignancies, solid organ transplantation, and targeted immunosuppressive therapies such as anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies (rituximab) and kinase inhibitors.

entities.name: Talaromyces marneffei
entities.description: Thermally dimorphic ascomycete fungus (formerly Penicillium marneffei) of the order Eurotiales and family Trichocomaceae, transitioning from mould at 25°C to yeast at 37°C.

entities.name: Thermal Dimorphism with Diffusible Wine-Red Pigment at 25C
entities.description: Pathognomonic phenotypic characteristic where the mould phase grown on Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25°C secretes a soluble, diffusible brick-red to wine-red pigment staining the reverse of the agar medium within 3-5 days.

entities.name: Intracellular Yeasts Dividing by Transverse Binary Fission Without Budding
entities.description: Pathognomonic parasitic tissue phase at 37°C consisting of unicellular, pleomorphic yeast cells (3–8 um) that reside inside host reticuloendothelial macrophages and divide exclusively by binary transverse fission (schizogony) with a central cross-wall septum, never by budding.

entities.name: Umbilicated Molluscum-Like Facial Papules with Central Necrotic Crater
entities.description: Primary visual hallmark present in 70% to 85% of patients at admission: crops of painless, non-pruritic, dome-shaped papules and nodules featuring a distinctive central necrotic depression, umbilication, or black hemorrhagic crust with prominent facial, neck, ear, and upper trunk predilection.

entities.name: Disseminated Reticuloendothelial Syndrome with Hepatosplenomegaly and Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Systemic constitutional syndrome characterized by high remittent or continuous fever (39–40°C), drenching night sweats, profound cachectic weight loss, generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy, and marked firm hepatosplenomegaly.

entities.name: Multifocal Osteolytic Bone Lesions and Subcutaneous Abscesses
entities.description: Severe destructive osteoarticular and soft tissue manifestations presenting with multiple osteolytic lesions (skull, ribs, long bones), septic arthritis, and subcutaneous cold abscesses, particularly prominent in non-HIV anti-IFN-gamma autoantibody patients.

entities.name: Pulmonary Reticulonodular Infiltrates and Alveolar Consolidation
entities.description: Respiratory involvement present in 50% to 60% of cases manifesting as productive cough, dyspnea, and hemoptysis, with radiographic evidence of diffuse bilateral interstitial reticulonodular opacities or alveolar consolidation.

entities.name: Touch Imprint Smear Demonstrating Transverse Septate Yeasts in Histiocytes
entities.description: Rapid bedside triage gold standard: Wright, Giemsa, or Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stained touch imprint smear or scraping of skin lesions demonstrating numerous intracellular (within histiocytes/macrophages) and extracellular 3–8 um yeasts displaying pathognomonic central transverse dividing septa.

entities.name: Rapid Fungal Culture Growth with Wine-Red Agar Diffusion at 25C
entities.description: Definitive culture confirmation: lysis-centrifugation blood culture or bone marrow aspirate culture yielding mould growth within 3 to 5 days at 25°C accompanied by deep brick-red to wine-red pigment diffusing into the agar medium.

entities.name: Profound Normocytic Anemia and Bicytopenia/Pancytopenia
entities.description: Admission complete blood count abnormalities including severe normocytic normochromic anemia (Hb < 7–8 g/dL), leukopenia (WBC < 3,000/uL), and thrombocytopenia (platelets < 50,000/uL) secondary to histiocytic bone marrow infiltration and hypersplenism.

entities.name: Marked Disproportionate Elevation of Serum Alkaline Phosphatase and GGT
entities.description: Admission liver chemistry demonstrating marked disproportionate cholestatic enzyme elevation (ALP and GGT 3–5x ULN) with mild-to-moderate AST/ALT transaminitis (2–3x ULN) resulting from diffuse granulomatous hepatic infiltration.

entities.name: Abdominal Ultrasound Demonstrating Hepatosplenomegaly with Microabscesses and Retroperitoneal Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Bedside abdominal point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) showing marked hepatosplenomegaly with multiple tiny (<1 cm) hypoechoic microabscesses and enlarged retroperitoneal/mesenteric lymph nodes (>1.5 cm).

entities.name: Chest Radiography Revealing Diffuse Bilateral Interstitial Reticulonodular Opacities
entities.description: Admission chest X-ray demonstrating diffuse bilateral reticulonodular interstitial opacities, patchy alveolar consolidation, localized cavitary lesions, and prominent hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Travel or Residence in Endemic Southeast Asia and Southern China
entities.description: Complete lack of travel or residence in the strictly restricted geographic endemic zones of Southeast Asia and southern China makes the diagnosis of talaromycosis virtually impossible.

entities.name: Microscopic Identification of Budding Yeasts Rather Than Binary Fission Septa
entities.description: Identification of budding yeasts (narrow-based or broad-based) on cytology, histopathology, or direct smear rules OUT Talaromyces marneffei, which reproduces strictly by transverse binary fission without budding.

entities.name: Absence of Thermal Dimorphism and Failure to Produce Soluble Red Pigment at 25C
entities.description: Failure of an isolated fungus to demonstrate temperature-dependent mould-to-yeast phase transition or absence of soluble brick-red/wine-red pigment diffusion at 25°C excludes Talaromyces marneffei.

entities.name: Normal CD4 Count in an Immunocompetent Patient Without Autoantibodies
entities.description: Preserved cell-mediated immunity with normal CD4 count (>500 cells/uL) in the absence of neutralizing anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies, immunosuppressive therapy, or malignancy makes disseminated talaromycosis exceptionally improbable.

entities.name: Disseminated Histoplasmosis
entities.description: Systemic dimorphic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, presenting in advanced HIV with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and skin lesions, but distinguished by narrow-based budding yeasts (2–4 um) and absence of red diffusible pigment on culture at 25°C.

entities.name: Disseminated Cryptococcosis
entities.description: Invasive fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus neoformans, presenting in advanced HIV with umbilicated facial papules and fever, but characterized by subacute meningoencephalitis with high opening pressure, positive cryptococcal antigen, and round encapsulated budding yeasts on India ink.

entities.name: Molluscum Contagiosum
entities.description: Cutaneous poxvirus infection presenting with dome-shaped umbilicated facial papules in advanced HIV, distinguished by purely superficial epidermal localization without systemic fever, wasting, organomegaly, cytopenias, or fungal elements, and biopsy showing Henderson-Paterson bodies.

entities.name: Miliary Tuberculosis
entities.description: Disseminated mycobacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis presenting with fever, cachexia, hepatosplenomegaly, and diffuse micronodular lung lesions in HIV, differentiated by acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain and typical absence of umbilicated necrotic facial papules.

entities.name: Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia
entities.description: Opportunistic fungal pulmonary infection presenting in advanced HIV with dyspnea, dry cough, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates, differentiated by disease confinement to lungs without cutaneous lesions, organomegaly, or fission yeasts.

entities.name: Intravenous Liposomal or Deoxycholate Amphotericin B Induction Therapy
entities.description: Evidence-based first-line 2-week induction regimen (liposomal amphotericin B 3–5 mg/kg/day or amphotericin B deoxycholate 0.7–1.0 mg/kg/day) demonstrated superior to itraconazole with faster blood fungal clearance, rapid defervescence, and >50% relative reduction in 2-week mortality.

entities.name: Oral Itraconazole Consolidation and Maintenance Prophylaxis
entities.description: Second-phase consolidation therapy (oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily with food for 10 weeks) followed by secondary maintenance prophylaxis (200 mg once daily) until sustained CD4 > 100 cells/uL on ART for at least 6 months.

entities.name: Early Antiretroviral Therapy Initiation Within One to Two Weeks
entities.description: Prompt initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) within 1 to 2 weeks after commencing amphotericin B therapy in HIV-infected patients, restoring cellular immunity with minimal risk of fatal IRIS.

entities.name: Universal Refractoriness to Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Agents
entities.description: Complete lack of clinical and microbiological response to broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, carbapenems), serving as an important clinical diagnostic clue for fungal infection.

relationships.target: Endemic Residence or Travel in Southeast Asia and Southern China
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, endemic zone, geographic restriction, Southeast Asia, southern China
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Talaromycosis is strictly restricted geographically to endemic regions of Southeast Asia and southern China (Thailand, Vietnam, southern China, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Taiwan, and northeastern India).

relationships.target: Agricultural Soil and Bamboo Rat Habitat Exposure During Rainy Season
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, bamboo rats, agricultural soil, monsoon, rainy season
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Environmental exposure to endemic reservoirs including agricultural soil and habitats of bamboo rats (Rhizomys pruinosus, Cannomys badius), with incidence peaking during the rainy/monsoon season.

relationships.target: Aerosol Inhalation of Environmental Conidia
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, conidia, aerosol, inhalation, respiratory entry
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Transmission occurs via inhalation of infectious aerosolized environmental conidia into the host respiratory tract.

relationships.target: Advanced HIV Infection with CD4 Count Below 100 cells/uL
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, advanced HIV, AIDS-defining infection, severe immunosuppression, CD4 under 100
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Over 80-90% of cases occur in patients with advanced HIV infection and severe immunosuppression characterized by CD4 counts below 100 cells/uL (typically <50 cells/uL).

relationships.target: High-Titer Neutralizing Anti-Interferon-Gamma Autoantibodies
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies, adult-onset immunodeficiency, non-HIV
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Non-HIV adult patients with high-titer neutralizing anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies suffer from severe, refractory disseminated talaromycosis with frequent osteolytic lesions.

relationships.target: Secondary Immunosuppression from Hematological Malignancies and Targeted Immunosuppressants
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, hematological malignancy, organ transplant, rituximab, kinase inhibitors
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Non-HIV immunosuppression resulting from hematological malignancies, solid organ transplantation, or treatment with targeted agents (rituximab, kinase inhibitors) predisposes to disseminated disease.

relationships.target: Talaromyces marneffei
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, Talaromyces marneffei, Penicillium marneffei, dimorphic fungus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Talaromycosis is caused etiologically by the thermally dimorphic ascomycete fungus Talaromyces marneffei (formerly Penicillium marneffei).

relationships.target: Thermal Dimorphism with Diffusible Wine-Red Pigment at 25C
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, thermal dimorphism, wine-red pigment, mould phase, 25C
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Talaromycosis exhibits thermal dimorphism, producing a mould phase at 25°C that secretes a soluble brick-red to wine-red diffusible pigment into agar media.

relationships.target: Intracellular Yeasts Dividing by Transverse Binary Fission Without Budding
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, binary fission, transverse septum, intracellular yeast, schizogony
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Talaromycosis is driven by parasitic yeast forms inside reticuloendothelial macrophages that replicate strictly by transverse binary fission across a cross-wall septum without budding.

relationships.target: Thermal Dimorphism with Diffusible Wine-Red Pigment at 25C
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, mould form, Sabouraud agar, red pigment secretion
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Talaromyces marneffei grows at 25°C as a filamentous sporulating mould that secretes a characteristic diffusible wine-red pigment on Sabouraud agar within 3-5 days.

relationships.target: Intracellular Yeasts Dividing by Transverse Binary Fission Without Budding
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, yeast phase, binary fission, non-budding, macrophage multiplication
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] In host tissue at 37°C, Talaromyces marneffei converts into an intracellular yeast dividing exclusively by transverse binary fission without forming buds.

relationships.target: Umbilicated Molluscum-Like Facial Papules with Central Necrotic Crater
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, umbilicated papules, necrotic crater, face
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Present in 70-85% of patients at admission, painless umbilicated papules with central necrotic crateriform depression or black crust on the face and trunk serve as the definitive clinical hallmark.

relationships.target: Disseminated Reticuloendothelial Syndrome with Hepatosplenomegaly and Lymphadenopathy
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, remittent fever, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, cachexia
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Manifests as a severe disseminated reticuloendothelial syndrome featuring high remittent fever (39-40°C), profound wasting, generalized lymphadenopathy, and firm hepatosplenomegaly.

relationships.target: Multifocal Osteolytic Bone Lesions and Subcutaneous Abscesses
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, osteolytic lesions, bone destruction, cold abscesses, anti-IFN-gamma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Multifocal osteolytic bone lesions of the skull, ribs, and long bones, accompanied by subcutaneous cold abscesses, form a prominent hallmark in non-HIV anti-IFN-gamma autoantibody patients.

relationships.target: Pulmonary Reticulonodular Infiltrates and Alveolar Consolidation
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, pulmonary infiltrates, cough, dyspnea, alveolar consolidation
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Pulmonary disease occurs in 50-60% of cases, presenting with productive cough, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and diffuse bilateral reticulonodular or alveolar infiltrates.

relationships.target: Touch Imprint Smear Demonstrating Transverse Septate Yeasts in Histiocytes
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, touch prep smear, skin scraping, transverse septum, Giemsa
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid bedside touch imprint or skin scraping stained with Wright/Giemsa reveals intracellular yeasts (3-8 um) displaying pathognomonic central transverse dividing septa within macrophages.

relationships.target: Rapid Fungal Culture Growth with Wine-Red Agar Diffusion at 25C
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, blood culture, bone marrow, wine-red pigment, lysis centrifugation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Fungal blood or bone marrow culture yields mould colonies within 3-5 days at 25°C accompanied by deep brick-red to wine-red pigment diffusing into the agar.

relationships.target: Profound Normocytic Anemia and Bicytopenia/Pancytopenia
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, pancytopenia, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, marrow suppression
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission CBC reveals severe normocytic normochromic anemia (Hb < 7-8 g/dL), leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia secondary to histiocytic marrow infiltration and hypersplenism.

relationships.target: Marked Disproportionate Elevation of Serum Alkaline Phosphatase and GGT
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, alkaline phosphatase, GGT, cholestatic pattern, hepatic granulomas
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum biochemistry reveals marked elevation of cholestatic enzymes (ALP and GGT 3-5x ULN) with modest transaminase elevation due to granulomatous hepatic parenchymal infiltration.

relationships.target: Abdominal Ultrasound Demonstrating Hepatosplenomegaly with Microabscesses and Retroperitoneal Lymphadenopathy
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, POCUS, abdominal ultrasound, microabscesses, lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside abdominal ultrasound demonstrates hepatosplenomegaly studded with tiny hypoechoic microabscesses (<1 cm) and enlarged retroperitoneal/mesenteric lymph nodes (>1.5 cm).

relationships.target: Chest Radiography Revealing Diffuse Bilateral Interstitial Reticulonodular Opacities
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, chest X-ray, reticulonodular opacities, mediastinal lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission chest radiograph shows diffuse bilateral interstitial reticulonodular opacities, patchy alveolar consolidation, and prominent hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

relationships.source: Touch Imprint Smear Demonstrating Transverse Septate Yeasts in Histiocytes
relationships.target: Intracellular Yeasts Dividing by Transverse Binary Fission Without Budding
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, microscopic visualization, transverse septum, macrophage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside touch imprint smear directly visualizes intracellular yeasts dividing by transverse binary fission with cross-walls inside macrophages.

relationships.source: Rapid Fungal Culture Growth with Wine-Red Agar Diffusion at 25C
relationships.target: Thermal Dimorphism with Diffusible Wine-Red Pigment at 25C
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, culture confirmation, wine-red pigment, agar diffusion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Blood or bone marrow culture confirms thermal dimorphism by growing filamentous colonies that secrete soluble wine-red pigment at 25°C.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Travel or Residence in Endemic Southeast Asia and Southern China
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, travel history, non-endemic, negative geographic exposure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of travel or residence in endemic Southeast Asia or southern China effectively rules out talaromycosis.

relationships.target: Microscopic Identification of Budding Yeasts Rather Than Binary Fission Septa
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, budding yeasts, absence of fission, narrow-based budding
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of budding fungal yeasts on cytological or histological examination rules out Talaromyces marneffei, which reproduces strictly by transverse binary fission.

relationships.target: Absence of Thermal Dimorphism and Failure to Produce Soluble Red Pigment at 25C
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, absence of red pigment, lack of dimorphism, monomorphic fungus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Lack of thermal dimorphism and failure to secrete diffusible wine-red pigment into agar medium at 25°C rules out Talaromyces marneffei.

relationships.target: Normal CD4 Count in an Immunocompetent Patient Without Autoantibodies
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal CD4 count, immunocompetent host, absent autoantibodies
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Disseminated talaromycosis is virtually ruled out in an immunocompetent host with normal CD4 count (>500 cells/uL) and no immunosuppressive risk factors or autoantibodies.

relationships.target: Disseminated Histoplasmosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Histoplasma capsulatum, narrow-based budding, absent red pigment
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Disseminated Histoplasmosis by Histoplasma's narrow-based budding yeasts (2-4 um) and lack of red pigment at 25°C, versus Talaromyces' transverse binary fission and diffusible wine-red pigment.

relationships.target: Disseminated Cryptococcosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Cryptococcus neoformans, meningitis, polysaccharide capsule, India ink
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Disseminated Cryptococcosis by Cryptococcus' predominant meningoencephalitis, encapsulated budding yeasts on India ink/mucicarmine, and positive CrAg, compared to non-encapsulated fission yeasts and dominant reticuloendothelial/skin pathology in Talaromyces.

relationships.target: Molluscum Contagiosum
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Molluscum contagiosum virus, Henderson-Paterson bodies, localized skin lesion
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Molluscum Contagiosum by Molluscum's purely localized superficial cutaneous restriction and intracytoplasmic Henderson-Paterson inclusion bodies, contrasting with Talaromyces' severe systemic illness, organomegaly, cytopenias, and fungal fission yeasts.

relationships.target: Miliary Tuberculosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, acid-fast bacilli, lack of umbilicated skin papules
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Miliary Tuberculosis by TB's acid-fast rod morphology on Ziehl-Neelsen stain and typical absence of umbilicated necrotic skin papules, compared to fungal fission yeasts on skin touch smears in Talaromycosis.

relationships.target: Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Pneumocystis jirovecii, pulmonary restricted, lack of mucocutaneous lesions
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia by PCP's lung-restricted presentation and trophic cyst morphology without umbilicated skin lesions, hepatosplenomegaly, or systemic dissemination.

relationships.target: Intravenous Liposomal or Deoxycholate Amphotericin B Induction Therapy
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, amphotericin B, induction therapy, mortality reduction, rapid defervescence
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Responds rapidly to intravenous amphotericin B induction (liposomal 3-5 mg/kg/day or deoxycholate 0.7-1.0 mg/kg/day) for 14 days, demonstrating superiority over itraconazole with faster blood fungal clearance and >50% relative reduction in 2-week mortality.

relationships.target: Oral Itraconazole Consolidation and Maintenance Prophylaxis
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, itraconazole, consolidation therapy, secondary prophylaxis, CD4 recovery
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Responds effectively to step-down oral itraconazole (200 mg twice daily with food for 10 weeks) for consolidation, followed by maintenance prophylaxis (200 mg once daily) until sustained CD4 > 100 cells/uL for at least 6 months on ART.

relationships.target: Early Antiretroviral Therapy Initiation Within One to Two Weeks
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, antiretroviral therapy, ART, immune reconstitution, early timing
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Clinical survival improves with early initiation of antiretroviral therapy within 1-2 weeks after starting amphotericin B, restoring cellular immunity with minimal risk of fatal IRIS.

relationships.target: Universal Refractoriness to Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Agents
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antibacterial refractoriness, beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, carbapenems
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Intrinsically unresponsive to all broad-spectrum antibacterial classes (beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, carbapenems), serving as a crucial clinical diagnostic clue for fungal etiology.
